top_rules: Module test harness MUST run every claimed CMake version line through a real provisioned binary, not an ambient `cmake` — find_ocx's 3.19 floor and Findocx.cmake's 3.15 are both untested claims.
Every inner configure a module's test harness drives MUST carry the configure gate (-Werror=dev/-Werror=author) — 5 of find_ocx's 10 test families skip it.
A negative test MUST assert the actual diagnostic (PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION or an expected-stderr file matched as regex), never a bare WILL_FAIL alone.
A reconfigure/memoization test MUST include a run that mutates an input and asserts invalidation, not just two identical configures asserting the cache hit (find_ocx's gap).

gersemi --check is SHOULD-grade and MUST always run with --definitions naming every file defining a custom command used by the target — a bare invocation on a module with helpers produces spurious warnings and under-formats real calls.

A module function whose keyword forwards a subcommand-and-flags list MUST carry '# gersemi: hints { KEYWORD: command_line }' — without it gersemi explodes every token onto its own line even with correct --definitions.

cmake_parse_arguments's fourth argument MUST be the literal ${ARGN} token, not a renamed variable, or gersemi's 'obvious manner' detector permanently fails for that function (find_ocx ocx.cmake:1327).
No shipped verification may cite cmake-lint/cmake-format as live (dead since 0.6.13, 2020-08-19); use gersemi as the only maintained formatter.
A verification grep/rg for presence/absence MUST NOT pipe into grep -q under set -o pipefail — reproduced live as a false negative (exit 141) on llvm-project despite thousands of real matches.
A verification scanning a whole repo MUST exclude vendored/generated trees (contrib/, third_party/, _deps/) by name unless the row is explicitly about vendored code.
surprises: gersemi run without --definitions doesn't just warn — it silently falls back to preserving original argument layout for every custom command, teaching authors it 'doesn't work' when a flag is missing.

Even WITH a correct --definitions pointer, gersemi still explodes a forwarded COMMAND-style keyword's tokens one-per-line unless the function definition carries an explicit '# gersemi: hints { KEYWORD: command_line }' comment — find_ocx has none.

--definitions is file-scoped, not project-scoped: pointing it at ocx.cmake alone still leaves 8 unknown-command warnings when checking CMakeLists.txt, because the test helpers live in a second file (tests/helpers.cmake) never named.

One of find_ocx's 6 cmake_parse_arguments call sites (ocx.cmake:1327, inside a dispatch-style ocx_index function) uses ${args} instead of the literal ${ARGN}, permanently defeating gersemi's detector for that function no matter what --definitions names.

cmake-conan does NOT test across multiple CMake versions at all (single pinned 3.31.7 via lukka/get-cmake) — contradicts the brief's framing of it as a 'test across CMake versions' exemplar; CPM.cmake is the real example (outer CI matrix: 3.16.3/3.28.3/4.3.2).

3 of the 7 exemplars carrying a .cmake-format config still actively run cmake_format==0.6.11 in live CI in 2026 (fmtlib/fmt, ModernCppStarter, CPMLicenses.cmake) — frozen-tool CI usage is real, not just a stray leftover config file.

top_rules: CMakeDeps+CMakeToolchain is the default generator pair; CMakeConfigDeps stays experimental at 2.32.0 despite incubating.rst calling it GA — the generator's own reference page still ships the experimental warning box
Never pair CMakeConfigDeps with find_package(... MODULE) — it permanently will not emit Find*.cmake modules, by design

Explicit `conan install` + `cmake --preset` is the documented default flow; the cmake-conan provider is for exceptional/IDE cases only, with 5 documented limits (MSVC/gcc/clang-only autodetect, first-find_package trigger, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE required, CMakeConfigDeps-only)
build_requires is a P0 finding (deprecated in Conan 2.28.0, 2026-04-28) — tool_requires is the only current form
A version range in requires/tool_requires must be paired with a committed conan.lock and an explicit --lockfile= flag in CI, since implicit pickup alone is invisible in CI logs

A cppstd or MSVC-runtime mismatch between a Conan profile and the CMake project is NOT diagnosed at configure time — measured on CMake 4.4.2: a later plain set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD) silently overrides the toolchain's injected value with zero warning at any level

CMakeUserPresets.json is skipped by Conan only if it already carries a vendor.conan key (measured from conan/tools/cmake/presets.py@2.32.0) — schema 3 for CMakePresets.json, schema 4 for CMakeUserPresets.json
Treat `from conans import` / `conan_basic_setup()` / `generators="cmake"` as a P0 Conan-1-residue finding, not a style nit — abseil-cpp's own live conanfile.py still has it
surprises: abseil/abseil-cpp's actual current conanfile.py (repo HEAD as fetched 2026-09-26) is unmigrated Conan-1 code (from conans import, conan_basic_setup(), generators="cmake") — a flagship, actively-maintained C++ library ships a recipe that cannot run under a Conan 2 client at all, self-admitted as 'best effort'

The two Conan doc pages disagreeing on CMakeConfigDeps status (incubating.rst says GA, cmakeconfigdeps.rst still ships the experimental warning include) is a live, still-unresolved contradiction as of the 2.32.0-era docs — the changelog never records a promotion past 'experimental' (2.25.0), so the reference page is the one that matches reality

Conan's own incubating.rst literally calls Workspaces 'generally available as experimental' in one sentence — not a wave-1 misreading but Conan's actual current phrasing, and three consecutive minors (2.29–2.31) still changed the conanws.py contract

The MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY generator-expression detection gap (cmake-conan#174) has been open, unfixed, for seven years (2019–2026) for a structural reason (the CMake default is itself a genex) — CCI's real workaround is to never read it back into Conan at all, only push Conan settings into a project-defined cache variable
CMakeConfigDeps needs no build_context_activated/build_context_suffix for tool_requires targets — a genuine ergonomic fix over CMakeDeps that gets lost in the 'still experimental' framing
CCI's own canonical package template still teaches CMakeDeps, not CMakeConfigDeps, as the recommended generator for a published recipe as of the 2.32.0 era

top_rules: MUST: a top-level manifest with versioning carries builtin-baseline or default-registry.baseline, else vcpkg silently runs unversioned Classic-mode resolution (no error).
MUST NOT: rely on overrides or vcpkg-configuration.json set inside a dependency's own manifest — only the top-level project's copy is ever honored.
MUST: set every VCPKG_* variable and CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE before the first project() call, since the vcpkg toolchain evaluates inside project().
MUST: chain a second toolchain only via VCPKG_CHAINLOAD_TOOLCHAIN_FILE, never a second -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=.

SHOULD: never let CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY disagree with the triplet's VCPKG_CRT_LINKAGE — measured: vcpkg's windows.cmake sets it via CACHE STRING with no FORCE, so a pre-existing value silently wins with zero configure-time diagnostic.

MUST: CI's VCPKG_BINARY_SOURCES never uses x-gha (removed outright, 'This feature has been removed from vcpkg'); every other x-prefixed provider needs an explicit experimental caveat every time it's cited.
SHOULD: offline/air-gapped CI sets X_VCPKG_ASSET_SOURCES with x-block-origin, else a cache miss silently falls through to the live upstream URL.

MUST NOT: a consuming project reference vcpkg-artifacts/vcpkg-ce/VCPKG_ARTIFACTS_* — announced removed after 2026-07-01 but measured still present and actively dependabot-patched as of the 2026-09-26 vcpkg-tool release.
surprises: vcpkg-tool shipped a new release on 2026-09-26 (today, published 06:19 UTC) — one past the era-recheck's 2026-07-27 figure; confirmed via the raw GitHub Releases API (the WebFetch summarizer's HTML read needed cross-checking) and full changelog read: no default-changing behavior found.

vcpkg-artifacts's 'will be removed after July 1' announcement (2026-05-27 release note) has not been executed: the /vcpkg-artifacts directory still exists in the live repo at the 2026-09-26 tag, still receives dependabot security bumps, and vcpkg-tool's own CMakePresets.json still carries VCPKG_ARTIFACTS_SHA/VCPKG_ARTIFACTS_DEVELOPMENT.

Measured a genuine, undocumented ABI trap: vcpkg's windows.cmake writes CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY as a plain 'CACHE STRING' with no FORCE, so a pre-existing cache entry (from a preset or -D flag) silently overrides the triplet's CRT-linkage choice with zero configure-time diagnostic — no doc page states this.

An unrecognized VCPKG_BINARY_SOURCES provider token is a hard parse error in vcpkg-tool source (msgUnknownBinaryProviderType), not a silent fallback to the files default — settles the map's open question in vcpkg's favor.

A full-tree filename search of vcpkg-tool's newest tag (2,461 paths) plus a grep of the checked-out vcpkg.cmake toolchain both confirm zero dependency-provider or CPS support anywhere in vcpkg, including no near-miss beyond an unrelated 'vcpkg package-info' CLI verb.

vcpkg-tool and the vcpkg registry are decoupled release trains: the tool tagged three times (one failed/unpromoted) since the registry's last tag on 2026-07-29 — a rule assuming version lockstep between them is wrong.

top_rules: MUST: one CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE source of record per configure leg — it is a single scalar, a second assignment silently overwrites the first.
MUST: never chain vcpkg's and Conan's generated toolchains in one configure — no primary source describes or supports the pairing (conan#12341 is the closest, and it redirects rather than endorses).

MUST: register a dependency provider only from a CMAKE_PROJECT_TOP_LEVEL_INCLUDES file, never a project's own CMakeLists.txt — Kitware's own words, plus a measured second-registration silently replacing the first with no error.

A hand-written cross toolchain chainloaded by vcpkg or Conan must be idempotent and side-effect-free — both already build re-entrancy guards (vcpkg's VCPKG_TOOLCHAIN early-return, Conan's try_compile block) around CMake re-reading the toolchain file on every try_compile.

Prefer Conan's tools.cmake.cmaketoolchain:user_toolchain over :toolchain_file when a cross toolchain must coexist with Conan — user_toolchain runs first and Conan still populates CMakeDeps wiring; :toolchain_file discards conan_toolchain.cmake entirely.

A vcpkg toolchain wired via a preset must put CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE/toolchainFile and every VCPKG_* variable in that same preset's cacheVariables, never a later CMakeLists.txt set() — anything after project() is a silent no-op.

When rules_foreign_cc wraps a project using a package manager's toolchain, pass it via cache_entries["CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE"] explicitly — rules_foreign_cc auto-skips its own crosstool synthesis when this is present, but omitting it lets its synthesized file silently replace the manager's settings.

The cmake-conan provider path (CMAKE_PROJECT_TOP_LEVEL_INCLUDES) never sets or reads CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE at all, so it composes with any toolchain by construction, not by convention — its README explicitly disclaims compiler/global settings.
A provider that must fire without an early find_package() needs cmake_language(DEFER ... CALL find_package ...) paired in — a real exemplar needed this exact workaround (cmake-conan#595).
VCPKG_CHAINLOAD_TOOLCHAIN_FILE has two unresolved, conflated meanings (project-scope vs triplet-scope) per an open vcpkg maintainer issue — never treat the two locations as equivalent.
surprises: Measured on CMake 4.4.2: two CMAKE_PROJECT_TOP_LEVEL_INCLUDES files both calling SET_DEPENDENCY_PROVIDER produce no error — the second silently replaces the first and only it is ever invoked, settling part of the map's wave-3-deferred M-H-03 question with a doc-plus-measurement combo rather than needing the staged dive.

The brief's cited rules_foreign_cc file foreign_cc/private/framework.bzl does not exist at the current corpus SHA (bb2f3e5d72) — the toolchain-composition logic moved to foreign_cc/private/cmake_script.bzl; any text still citing framework.bzl for this logic is stale.

vcpkg.cmake is self-guarding by design (VCPKG_TOOLCHAIN flag, early return on re-entry), which is what makes it safe under try_compile's per-check toolchain re-read — this mechanism was undocumented in vcpkg's own prose and only visible by reading the source.

The cmake-conan dependency-provider flow and any CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE never collide by construction (the provider literally never reads or writes that variable) — composition here is a non-problem, unlike every other pairing in this dive.

conan-io/conan#12341 shows Conan deliberately chose NOT to build a vcpkg-style generic chainload toolchain, redirecting the request to the (separately shipped) dependency-provider architecture instead — the two ecosystems' toolchain philosophies diverged on purpose, not by oversight.

A real exemplar (aminya/project_options) already hand-rolled the CMAKE_PROJECT_TOP_LEVEL_INCLUDES list-append plus cmake_language(DEFER) workaround for cmake-conan's find_package-only visibility, years before this being documented as a general pattern.

top_rules: A git-fetched dependency states a full 40-hex GIT_TAG; branch/HEAD is MUST-fail, a semver tag is SHOULD-fail — CMake 4.4.2's own docs already say hash over branch.
URL-form FetchContent_Declare/ExternalProject_Add always carries URL_HASH — duckdb/duckdb's DuckDBCppApi.cmake is a real, current counterexample with none.
A checksum variable may resolve outside any .cmake file (arrow's cpp/thirdparty/versions.txt) — a --include='*.cmake' grep alone can't verify a pin is checked.

An opaque ${VAR} GIT_TAG or macro parameter must be resolved at its set() or leaf call sites before judging it — duckdb resolves to real hashes at all 23 sites, curl resolves to a floating 'master' default; identical at the declare site.

CPMAddPackage real adopters mostly use version tags, not commit hashes, despite CPM's own README recommending hashes — only a bare branch name (GIT_TAG 'main') is the MUST finding, seen in cpp-best-practices/cmake_template.
CPM sets CMP0077/CMP0126/CMP0135/CMP0150 to NEW unconditionally on load (confirmed at cpm-cmake/CPM.cmake@01678cfe17:91,96,103,109) — flag this to any consumer relying on OLD behavior.
vcpkg_cmake_configure unconditionally injects -DFETCHCONTENT_FULLY_DISCONNECTED=ON for every CMake-based port — the offline switch is package-manager-enforced, not per-portfile, in that ecosystem.
A submodule's branch= key never means 'floats' by itself (ClickHouse's own .gitmodules says so explicitly); Boost's branch = . is a non-standard tooling convention, not a real branch.
surprises: curl/curl's own CMake test harness defaults FROM_GIT_TAG to the literal "master" (option(FROM_GIT_TAG "Git tag" "master")) — a real floating-branch default hiding behind what looked like an opaque variable.
grpc/grpc's own teaching example pins GIT_TAG to the literal placeholder string "vGRPC_TAG_VERSION_OF_YOUR_CHOICE" — not a valid git ref at all, would fail if copy-pasted verbatim.

duckdb/duckdb's register_external_extension macro takes GIT_TAG as an opaque parameter that looks unpinned at the definition, but resolves to a real 40-hex commit at all 23 real call sites — the opposite failure mode from curl's.

apache/arrow's entire 46-checksum thirdparty pin set lives in a plain-text cpp/thirdparty/versions.txt, not any .cmake file, so a --include='*.cmake' grep would completely miss where the pins actually are.
OpenSSF Scorecard's Pinned-Dependencies check still has zero awareness of CMake, FetchContent or CPM as of 2026-09-26 — confirmed directly from its own docs, not just carried forward from wave 1.

A naive 'file(DOWNLOAD) = network at configure time' grep has a confirmed false positive: glfw/glfw's GenerateMappings.cmake only runs via a build-time add_custom_command(cmake -P ...), never during configure.

top_rules: Before calling a dual repo 'no sync,' check ci/ and tools/internal_ci/ for Kokoro-driven CMake+Bazel scripts, not just .github/workflows/ — abseil and googletest hide their real sync there
Downgrade a build-only Bazel/CMake CI job (no test step) to PARTIAL sync, never round it up to FULL — Catch2 and gflags build both but test only CMake

When CMakeLists.txt or a .cmake file carries an auto-generated header, read the named generator before comparing versions — grpc and protobuf generate their CMake side from Bazel, so matching versions mean generation, not luck
A per-pair drift check must report NOT KNOWABLE STATICALLY when the CMake side's find_package/FetchContent carries no version at all (re2's absl/gtest), never silently pass an empty diff
Never derive a Bazel label from a CMake namespaced target by pattern — verify both sides; 6 of 8 measured pairs mismatch (ZLIB::ZLIB vs @zlib//:z, protobuf::libprotobuf vs @protobuf//:protobuf)

For Conan under Bzlmod (Bazel ≥7.2/9), wire BazelDeps via include("//conan:conan_deps.MODULE.bazel") in the root MODULE.bazel — never local_path_override, and it only works for the Bazel root module, not a BCR-published library

A git-submodule-pinned CMake dependency (mode 160000) is never comparable to a bazel_dep version string without resolving the submodule commit to an upstream tag first — report it blocked, not 'no drift detected'
Never claim vcpkg has a Bazel-export generator (no rules_vcpkg, no vcpkg export --format=bazel) — the only vcpkg/Bazel hits run the opposite direction or are a port stale since 2022
surprises: abseil-cpp and googletest have ZERO GitHub Actions workflow files yet fully sync CMake+Bazel via Kokoro-triggered ci/*.sh scripts — the audit's 'no sync' count was wrong because it only checked .github/workflows
The true 'no dual-build CI sync' count is 3 (yaml-cpp, zlib, nlohmann/json), not the audit's 5 or 4 — and nlohmann/json was never named by the audit at all

protobuf's cmake/dependencies.cmake is literally auto-generated from MODULE.bazel via a genrule + staleness_test — the strongest 'keep two dependency graphs in sync' mechanism in the corpus, though its staleness test is tags=["manual"] and not found wired into any GH Actions workflow
grpc's CMakeLists.txt is generated FROM Bazel BUILD metadata (extract_metadata_from_bazel_xml.py), never the reverse — settles the brief's 'does it also generate BUILD files' question as no

Conan's BazelDeps DOES work under Bzlmod/Bazel 9 today via a generated conan_deps.MODULE.bazel + include() — the topic map's conflict 19 suspicion (docs vs changelog can't both be true) resolves because the Bzlmod path is documented on a different reference page than the one first checked

Two concrete version-drift examples exist but both are minor-version, not major (yaml-cpp: CMake vendors gtest 1.16.0 vs Bazel's 1.17.0.bcr.2; benchmark: CMake fetches gtest v1.15.2 vs Bazel's 1.14.0, drift running the opposite direction) — no major-version split found in the corpus at these SHAs

top_rules: Configure gate is two lines by version: -Werror=dev/deprecated on ≤4.3, -Werror=author/deprecated on 4.4+; -Werror=author is silently a no-op on ≤4.3.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION min...max) needs exactly three literal dots; two dots (yaml-cpp's real CMakeLists.txt:1) silently degrades to VERSION min alone with zero diagnostic, even under -Werror=dev on 4.4.2.

CACHE INTERNAL implies FORCE (confirmed by execution) — find_ocx's __ocx_set_result memo write is correct; the audit's headline 'stale memo' defect is refuted by a 3-run reconfigure repro (run3 memo_hit=TRUE).

A function's policy behavior is fixed at its definition line, not its call line: a function defined after a module's cmake_policy(POP) silently inherits the includer's policy version instead of the module's pin (find_ocx's __ocx_self_update at ocx.cmake:1383).

cmake_parse_arguments via unquoted ${ARGN} forwarding has two measured bugs PARSE_ARGV lacks: it silently drops an explicit empty-string argument, and it splits a semicolon-bearing single value across the keyword and UNPARSED_ARGUMENTS.
file(DOWNLOAD ...) of a failed file:// URL never stops configure (exit 0) with or without STATUS, and without STATUS produces zero diagnostic text — always capture and check STATUS.

include_guard(GLOBAL) keys on the including file's own absolute path, so two vendored copies of 'the same' module at different paths both execute in full with no collision warning — needs its own version-assertion guard.
Presets schema ≥12 rejects warnings.dev with an explicit error on 4.4.2 ('File version must be 11 or lower for warnings.dev support'); schema ≤11 keeps warnings.dev working unchanged.

CMD_UNINITIALIZED and CMD_INSTALL_ABSOLUTE_DESTINATION default to ignore and have no parent category, so -Werror=author/dev never promotes them — a strict gate must name -Werror=uninitialized and -Werror=install-absolute-destination explicitly.

return(PROPAGATE ...) inside a bare block() at a project's own top-level CMakeLists.txt only warns ('current scope has no parent') and silently skips the rest of the file — never use it outside a function or a subdirectory listfile.
surprises: 4.4.2 still accepts -Werror=dev as a deprecated synonym for -Werror=author and prints an unconditional one-line deprecation notice that no -W flag can gate or suppress.

yaml-cpp's real, current CMakeLists.txt:1 (`VERSION 3.15..4.3`, two dots not three) is not a range at all — it silently collapses to VERSION 3.15 with zero warning on any of the three binaries, even under -Werror=dev/author; this is a live authoring defect in a widely-used exemplar, not a historical one.

Unquoted ${ARGN} forwarding into cmake_parse_arguments silently erases an explicit empty-string argument before parsing ever sees it, making `VALUE ""` indistinguishable from omitting VALUE entirely — a distinct bug from the known semicolon-splitting issue, and neither reproduces under PARSE_ARGV.

return(PROPAGATE var) inside a block(SCOPE_FOR VARIABLES) at the very top of a project's root CMakeLists.txt doesn't just fail to propagate — it silently truncates the entire remainder of the listfile, because a directory-scope return() exits the file and a bare block() doesn't intercept that.

Two different files both calling include_guard(GLOBAL) are never deduplicated against each other (the guard keys on the including file's own path), so two vendored copies of a module both run in full with zero diagnostic of the collision — not the false sense of protection the pattern implies.

option()'s existing-cache-entry handling coerces only the TYPE field to BOOL, not the VALUE, so a -DVAR=non-boolean-string cache entry can persist under an option()-declared BOOL type with no coercion or warning.

top_rules: CMK-BZL-01 (MUST): wrapped project must reach zero network at configure or build; measured — FetchContent fails cleanly under unshare -rn on CMake 4.4.2
CMK-BZL-02 (MUST): install() must produce every out_* name at a stable path under CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX; verify by diffing a fresh-prefix install listing against the declared out_* set
CMK-BZL-03 (MUST): install() destinations must honor CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX, never a hardcoded absolute path
CMK-BZL-04 (MUST): a caller-supplied CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE must be honored, never clobbered — measured: toolchain file's CMAKE_C_COMPILER reaches the project unmodified

CMK-BZL-05 (SHOULD): a static lib must accept PIC via compiler flags, not require CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE as a cache entry — measured 3-way (no-PIC fails link into .so; POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON fixes it; -fPIC via CMAKE_C_FLAGS alone also fixes it, the mechanism rules_foreign_cc 0.16.0 actually uses per PR #1440)
CMK-BZL-06 (MUST): static/shared selection must be driven by BUILD_SHARED_LIBS via cache_entries, never hardcoded STATIC/SHARED
CMK-BZL-08 (MUST): no installed Config.cmake/.pc file may embed an absolute build-tree path — measured empty grep against a fresh-prefix install

CMK-BZL-09 (SHOULD): don't design package metadata around CPS — rules_foreign_cc's own bundled CMake provisioning tops out at 4.0.7 (unchanged at 0.16.0/bb2f3e5d72), so install(PACKAGE_INFO) (CMake >=4.3) is dead code under the rule's default and documented overrides
surprises: The default bundled CMake ceiling (3.19.8-4.0.7, default 3.31.12) is completely unchanged at rules_foreign_cc 0.16.0/bb2f3e5d72 despite the era-recheck flagging a 'version model shift' — the hub-and-spoke registration rewrite changed only the internal plumbing, not the actual numbers; confirmed by reading cmake_versions.bzl, repositories.bzl and MODULE.bazel at the new SHA.

That ceiling means CPS (install(PACKAGE_INFO), stable at CMake 4.3.0) can never execute under rules_foreign_cc's own bundled CMake at all — every version the rule can provision predates 4.1. This is a structural dead-end, not a lag the next release is likely to close.

rules_foreign_cc 0.16.0 (2026-09-15, ending a ~15-month tagging gap) shipped a fix for issue #421 (PR #1440, merged 2025-11-06) that delivers PIC as an injected compiler flag via cc_toolchain_util.bzl's use_pic, not via a CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE cache entry — yet issue #421 is still open on the tracker, a bookkeeping lag not evidence of an incomplete fix.

Issues #329 (parallel-build passthrough) and #1129 (symlinked install outputs) are both still open with no movement since wave 1, one dating back to 2019 — stable non-fixes worth encoding as permanent caller responsibilities rather than 'pending' rows.

0.16.0 quietly added experimental_validate_outputs_in_action (default True) which now validates a wrapped build's expected outputs before the action exits — new safety net for BZL-CC-23's output-side check that didn't exist in wave 1's f68b351c46 snapshot.

rules_foreign_cc's own canonical worked example (examples/cmake_crosstool) wraps a CMakeLists.txt pinned to cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8.4) — the ruleset's own documentation is not a version-floor exemplar and must not be cited as one.

top_rules: Every Find<Pkg>.cmake MUST set <Pkg>_FOUND via find_package_handle_standard_args and guard every imported target with if(NOT TARGET ...) (M-D-03)
Every file(DOWNLOAD) MUST check STATUS, hash executable content, and pass TLS_VERIFY ON explicitly below CMake 3.31 -- MEASURED: a failed download does not fail configure by itself (M-D-05)
Every execute_process() MUST check RESULT_VARIABLE or pass COMMAND_ERROR_IS_FATAL ANY -- MEASURED: an unchecked failing child process does not fail configure (M-D-06)
A module snapshotting env vars into CACHE MUST exclude credential-shaped names -- MEASURED: a naive snapshot wrote a planted token into CMakeCache.txt in plaintext (M-D-10)

A provisioning module MUST prime find_package with the case-preserved <Name>_ROOT only, never the upper-case CMP0144 form -- MEASURED: case-preserved alone suffices and outranks CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH (M-D-12)
A Find module that fetches on a miss (ccache's FindZstd.cmake) MUST document and gate that fetch behind an off-by-default opt-in, never fetch silently (M-D-04)

Default to function(); reach for macro() only when the call's whole purpose is to mutate the caller's scope -- every macro in this sample (find_ocx, CPM, project_options) is justified this way, none is habit (M-C-04)
A self-updating/copy-and-own module MUST hash-verify the final artifact before it replaces anything on disk and expose a consumer-readable version (M-D-14)
surprises: cpm-cmake/CPM.cmake permanently mutates four CMAKE_POLICY_DEFAULT_CMPxxxx variables at include time with no PUSH/POP anywhere in the file -- a global, undocumented-in-tutorials side effect of the most widely used third-party CMake helper in the corpus

A module's <Name>_ROOT hint only activates find_package's search-roots stack from inside an actual find_package() call -- a bare find_path() at top level ignores it entirely, an easy thing to measure wrong
The upper-case <NAME>_ROOT form (CMP0144) is the consumer's opt-in, not something the provisioning module needs to also emit -- a plausible AI mistake this dive corrects by measurement
Even Conan's own actively-maintained conan_provider.cmake has one unchecked execute_process (a macOS xcrun probe) -- a narrow, defensible exception to the fail-loud rule
ccache's shipped FindZstd.cmake breaks three cmake-developer(7) conventions in one 82-line file: no FPHSA, a non-namespaced imported target, and a silent FetchContent fallback on a miss

The audit's headline find_ocx defect (CACHE INTERNAL without FORCE) was already refuted upstream (host H4); this dive does not repeat it and instead surfaces the CPM.cmake finding as the sharper 'breaks its own contract' surprise

top_rules: Never pass both FIND_PACKAGE_ARGS and OVERRIDE_FIND_PACKAGE to one FetchContent_Declare — hard FATAL_ERROR on 3.31.12 and 4.4.2, not a soft precedence choice.
FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_<X> outranks everything — with it set, find_package/FIND_PACKAGE_ARGS/CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH/providers are all bypassed entirely (measured).

Scope CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM fixes locally (save/set/restore around one FetchContent call) — global -D or environment forms mask the CMake-4.0 floor-removal check for the whole tree, and the environment form silently persists in the cache after being unset.

project(...
